block.comment: Purpose: Send a dashboard JSON header once, then stream values for its widgets. Hardware: use Connections to check pin ownership for your selected board. Open the comment bubbles on the main steps for explanations.
Send the dashboard JSON before ordinary data rows. Click this compact message field to edit the formatted JSON. Plotter creates the widgets; Arduino only prints text.
Runs once after power-on or reset. Initialise the program here; repeating measurements and animation belong in loop.
Measure the voltage on this analog input. On ATmega168/328, the ADC returns 0–1023; other boards may use a different ADC range. A potentiometer wiper or analog sensor connects here.
Wait for the given number of milliseconds (1000 ms = 1 second). This pauses the main program; avoid long waits when loop must service motors, music files or serial input.
Send this value/text to the computer. A new line finishes one record; same line can build a record from several values. Match Monitor/Plotter baud to the sketch.

Create sample as uint16_t. Outside a body it is global; inside a function/setup/loop it belongs to that body. Its value input is the initial value.
Repeats until power is removed. Each block runs in order, then execution returns to the top. Keep this loop responsive when servicing motors, music or serial input.
